title: Your first Vitest check
summary: Vitest runs named tests and reports mismatched expectations. It works with JavaScript and TypeScript projects.
introduction: Vitest runs named tests and reports mismatched expectations. It works with JavaScript and TypeScript projects. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Vitest runs named tests and reports mismatched expectations. It works with JavaScript and TypeScript projects.

blocks.title: Before you start
blocks.text: These are test-file examples for a local project with Vitest installed. They do not run in this site's plain JavaScript sandbox. Use the official setup guide with a teacher if needed.
This course teaches the basics. It does not cover every feature of Vitest. Keep real personal data and secret keys out of practice files.

blocks.code:
import { test, expect, vi, beforeEach, afterEach } from "vitest";
test("counts apples", () => { expect(3 + 2).toBe(5); });
blocks.title: Your first Vitest check

blocks.text: This test passes because the total is 5.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Change the expected total and read the mismatch.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: These imports belong in a Vitest test file, not a plain browser script.
For more detail later, use this [Vitest further reading](https://vitest.dev/guide/).
